<?php

$stdin = fopen("php://stdin", "r");
$input = fgets($stdin);
$parts = explode(" ", trim($input));

$n = (int)$parts[0];
$k = (int)$parts[1];

if ($k <= $n + 1) {
    echo (int)(($k - 1) / 2) . "\n";
    exit;
}

if ($k >= $n * 2) {
    echo "0\n";
    exit;
}

// Both branches in Kotlin do the same calculation: n - k / 2 (integer division)
echo ($n - (int)($k / 2)) . "\n";

- Print using `echo` or `print`.

source_data.prob_desc_description: Tanechka is shopping in the toy shop. There are exactly $$$n$$$ toys in the shop for sale, the cost of the $$$i$$$-th toy is $$$i$$$ burles. She wants to choose two toys in such a way that their total cost is $$$k$$$ burles. How many ways to do that does she have?Each toy appears in the shop exactly once. Pairs $$$(a, b)$$$ and $$$(b, a)$$$ are considered equal. Pairs $$$(a, b)$$$, where $$$a=b$$$, are not allowed.
source_data.prob_desc_output_spec: Print the number of ways to choose the pair of toys satisfying the condition above. Print 0, if Tanechka can choose no pair of toys in such a way that their total cost is $$$k$$$ burles.
source_data.prob_desc_input_spec: The first line of the input contains two integers $$$n$$$, $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \le n, k \le 10^{14}$$$) — the number of toys and the expected total cost of the pair of toys.
source_data.prob_desc_notes: NoteIn the first example Tanechka can choose the pair of toys ($$$1, 4$$$) or the pair of toys ($$$2, 3$$$).In the second example Tanechka can choose only the pair of toys ($$$7, 8$$$).In the third example choosing any pair of toys will lead to the total cost less than $$$20$$$. So the answer is 0.In the fourth example she can choose the following pairs: $$$(1, 1000000000000)$$$, $$$(2, 999999999999)$$$, $$$(3, 999999999998)$$$, ..., $$$(500000000000, 500000000001)$$$. The number of such pairs is exactly $$$500000000000$$$.
